Subjective: Ishidzu, a one and a half year old dog, presented with symptoms of head shaking and holding the head tilted to the left side for 2-3 days. The owner reports decreased appetite during this period.
Objective: Physical examination revealed a foreign body in the left ear and yeast infection in the right ear. Ear cleaning was performed. Current medications include Cefpodoxime syrup 3ml orally, continued from prior treatment.
Assessment: Foreign body in the left ear with concurrent yeast infection in the right ear causing otitis externa. Symptoms include head shaking, head tilt, and decreased appetite likely secondary to ear discomfort and infection.
Plan: Continue Cefpodoxime syrup orally for an additional 5-7 days. Administer Easotic ear drops once daily for 5 days. Monitor response to treatment. If symptoms persist or worsen, perform ear swab for culture and sensitivity to guide further therapy.
Conclusion: Ishidzu is being treated for bilateral ear infections with foreign body and yeast involvement. Treatment is ongoing with antibiotics and antifungal ear drops. Follow-up is necessary to ensure resolution.
DifferentialDiagnosis: Otitis externa due to foreign body and yeast infection; possible secondary bacterial infection; consider otitis media if symptoms persist.
KeyIssues: Foreign body in left ear, yeast infection in right ear, head shaking, head tilt, decreased appetite.
AbnormalFindings: Foreign body detected in left ear; yeast growth in right ear; head tilt to left side; decreased appetite.
CustomerInstructions: Administer Cefpodoxime syrup 3ml orally as directed for 5-7 more days. Apply Easotic ear drops once daily for 5 days. Observe for improvement in head shaking and appetite. Return for re-evaluation if no improvement or worsening occurs.
Protocols: Ear cleaning performed. Antibiotic therapy with Cefpodoxime syrup continued. Antifungal treatment with Easotic ear drops initiated. Culture and sensitivity planned if no improvement.
Reminders: Monitor for signs of worsening infection or discomfort. Schedule follow-up appointment after completion of medication course. Consider ear swab culture if symptoms persist.
